formalDefinition: {<M,X,Y,Z> | M is a subset of X*Y*Z,|X|=|Y|=|Z| and a subset of M, M', exists, where |M'| = |A|,|B|,|C|, and no two elements of M' agree in any cooridinate}
problemDefinition: 3-Dimensional Matching is when, given 3 equally sized sets, X, Y, and Z, and a set of constraints M, being a subset of XxYxZ, are you able to select a set of constraints which contain each element of X, Y, and Z in one and only one 3-tuple.
inputDescription: X, Y, and Z, three equally sized sets, and M, a set of 3-tuple constraints over X x Y x Z
outputDescription: True or False, whether a subset of M exists that matches every element of X, Y, and Z exactly once
source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
instanceFormat: Format: {x1,...}{y1,...}{z1,...}{x,y,z},... | X,Y,Z are the three sets, followed by one 3-tuple per constraint in M Example: {Paul,Sally,Dave}{Madison,Austin,Bob}{Chloe,Frank,Jake}{Paul,Madison,Chloe}{Paul,Austin,Jake}{Sally,Bob,Chloe}{Sally,Madison,Frank}{Dave,Austin,Chloe}{Dave,Bob,Chloe}
certificateFormat: Format: {x,y,z}{x,y,z}... | tuples from M that together contain every element of X, Y and Z exactly once Example: {Paul,Austin,Jake}{Sally,Madison,Frank}{Dave,Bob,Chloe}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for 3-Dimensional Matching. It enumerates every combination of |X| triples from M and returns the first one that is a perfect matching.

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This verifier checks that a certificate is a perfect matching: every triple is one of the constraints in M, no element of X, Y or Z is used twice, and every element of X, Y and Z is covered.

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: Draws X, Y and Z as three columns and each triple of M as a line through one element of each. A perfect matching picks triples that together use every element exactly once; a set of triples that uses an element twice fails.
